title: Memory optimization for small-language-model-driven security agents
audience: Final review panel: internal faculty examiner and an industry examiner. Know security and software engineering, have not read this codebase.
goal: Convince the panel the work is complete, measured, honest about its limits, and technically contributed by all three students.
register: technical and exact; short declarative sentences; identifiers and tool names in mono
direction: Terminal Noir, phosphor accent #7CFF6B on near-black, Geist display and JetBrains Mono labels

claims.text: Project title: Memory optimization for small-language-model-driven security agents
claims.quote: MEMORY OPTIMIZATION FOR SMALL-LANGUAGE-MODEL-DRIVEN SECURITY AGENTS

claims.text: Madhan T B 23BCE1087, Manikandan S 23BCE1476, Sushindh A 23BCE1513
claims.quote: MADHAN T B (23BCE1087)

claims.text: Manikandan S 23BCE1476 and Sushindh A 23BCE1513
claims.quote: MANIKANDAN S (23BCE1476)

claims.text: Sushindh A 23BCE1513
claims.quote: SUSHINDH A (23BCE1513)

claims.text: Hosted models strong enough for the job need target names, banners, credentials and raw tool output sent to a third party
claims.quote: the hosted models strong enough to do the job need target names, banners, credentials and raw tool output sent to a third party, and an engagement contract usually forbids that data from leaving the client

claims.text: What stays human is the judgement that sequences the tools
claims.quote: What stays human is the judgement that sequences them, reads what a result means and keeps track of what has already been ruled out.

claims.text: A real request overflowed a 16384 token context window by about 1300 tokens
claims.quote:
a real request still overflowed
#: the server's actual context window ("17245 tokens... n_ctx: 16384") by
#: ~1300 tokens despite fitting this budget

claims.text: The model can supply direction only when memory, grounding, phase discipline and pre-execution policy come from the system around it
claims.quote: The model can supply direction, but only when memory, grounding, phase discipline and pre-execution policy come from the system around it instead of from the model itself.

claims.text: The agent is a LangGraph state machine with six nodes: think, act, extract, route, remember and respond
claims.quote: The agent is a LangGraph state machine with six nodes: think, act, extract, route, remember and respond.

claims.text: AgentEvent is the union alias over 15 event types
claims.quote: `AgentEvent` is the union alias over those fifteen types.

claims.text: State persists across submit() calls within one process via a MemorySaver checkpointer
claims.quote:
State — messages, DEPG nodes/edges, memory items, phase — persists across
`submit()` calls within one process

claims.text: Six PTES phases: recon, enumeration, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, post exploitation, reporting
claims.quote:
class Phase(Enum):
    RECON = 1
    ENUMERATION = 2
    VULNERABILITY_DISCOVERY = 3
    EXPLOITATION = 4
    POST_EXPLOITATION = 5
    REPORTING = 6

claims.text: Recon may only move to recon or enumeration
claims.quote: Phase.RECON: frozenset({Phase.RECON, Phase.ENUMERATION})

claims.text: Reporting is terminal
claims.quote: Phase.REPORTING: frozenset({Phase.REPORTING})

claims.text: transition() is the single choke point every phase change goes through
claims.quote:
`PhaseStateMachine`'s
  `transition()` is the single choke point every phase change goes through.

claims.text: The agent caps AI turns at 2 per user turn
claims.quote: MAX_AI_TURNS = 2

claims.text: The token estimate uses 3 characters per token
claims.quote: _CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3

claims.text: 512 tokens are reserved for the response
claims.quote: _RESPONSE_RESERVE_TOKENS = 512

claims.text: The default context window is 32768 tokens
claims.quote: DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 32_768

claims.text: Tier 1 shrinks old tool output to a 350 character head and a 100 character tail
claims.quote:
_OLD_TOOL_OUTPUT_HEAD_CHARS = 350
_OLD_TOOL_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS = 100

claims.text: Flat per message overhead is 4 tokens
claims.quote: _PER_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD_TOKENS = 4

claims.text: Three tiers, cheapest sufficient wins, each engaging once the one before it could not fit the budget or left usage above the proactive threshold
claims.quote:
Three tiers, cheapest-sufficient wins, each engaging once the one
    before it either couldn't fit the budget or left usage above
    _PROACTIVE_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD

claims.text: A plain character cut landed inside the word valid in a hydra run and inverted a negative result
claims.quote:
a plain char-count cut landed inside the word "valid"
#: in a failed hydra run's own "0 valid password found" line, leaving a
#: tail of "d password found" — read by the model as a positive hit,
#: inverting a negative result.

claims.text: Full history stays in state; compaction only shapes what is sent to the model
claims.quote: Full history stays in state — this only shapes what's sent to the model.

claims.text: One real token counter call catches an overshoot before the prompt is sent
claims.quote:
One real token_counter call (when
#: available) catches an overshoot before this turn's prompt is sent,
#: not after.

claims.text: DEPG and memory context is rebuilt fresh from state every think() call, not from the compacted history
claims.quote: rebuilt fresh from state every think() call, not from this history.

claims.text: 9 real tools execute only through one sandboxed, argv only seam behind a hard allowlist
claims.quote: Nine real tools execute only through one sandboxed, argv-only seam behind a hard allowlist

claims.text: The eight declared tools are nikto, whatweb, dnsenum, nmap, curl, sqlmap, gobuster and wafw00f
claims.quote: the 8 declared tools: nikto, whatweb, dnsenum, nmap, curl, sqlmap, gobuster, wafw00f

claims.text: A destructive tool is registered but unreachable in every phase until an explicit phases key is added
claims.quote:
writes / executes / destructive -> NONE — registered but unreachable in
#                                      every phase until you add an explicit
#                                      `phases:` key.

claims.text: A guardrail chain blocks out of scope targets, dangerous arguments and phase illegal tools before any process is spawned
claims.quote: a guardrail chain blocks out-of-scope targets, dangerous arguments and phase-illegal tools before any process is spawned

claims.text: Every real tool runs with argv only execution, a per call scratch directory and a timeout that kills the whole process tree
claims.quote:
argv-only execution
  (never `shell=True`), a per-call scratch directory that no longer exists
  once the call returns, and a hard timeout that kills the whole process
  tree, not just the leaf

claims.text: hydra's wordlist arguments only ever select one of two fixed, named wordlists, never an arbitrary path
claims.quote: only ever select one of two fixed, named wordlists

claims.text: Container ceilings: 2 GB memory, 2 GB swap, 2 processors, 512 processes
claims.quote: 2 GB memory, 2 GB swap, 2 processors, 512 processes

claims.text: The inference key arrives as a read only mounted file and not an environment variable
claims.quote: The inference key arrives as a read-only mounted file and not an environment variable, because an environment variable is visible at the container layer.

claims.text: A claim the model cannot ground against real tool text is demoted instead of reported
claims.quote: so a claim the model cannot ground against real tool text is demoted instead of reported

claims.text: Graph merges nodes and edges, resolves each dirty node's state via reduce_state, and prunes fully dead regions
claims.quote:
is the container that merges nodes/edges as they're
  proposed, resolves each dirty node's `state` via `reduce_state`
  (`depg/reducer.py`), and prunes fully-dead regions.

claims.text: normalize_target collapses 10.0.0.5, ssh://10.0.0.5:22 and 10.0.0.5. onto one node family
claims.quote:
so
  `10.0.0.5`/`ssh://10.0.0.5:22`/`10.0.0.5.` collapse onto one node family
  instead of fragmenting.

claims.text: generality is the share of this run's targets that already produced this cause class, and downstream is the descendant count
claims.quote:
`generality` (cross-target transfer: what share of this run's targets already produced this
  cause_class) and `downstream` (descendant count)

claims.text: Graded propagation uses a noisy OR over parents and is opt in
claims.quote: Noisy-OR over parents (a node needs *any* live precondition)

claims.text: The memory salience score is S = w_tier times s0 times e to the minus lambda age, plus beta times hits
claims.quote: f"S = w_tier · s₀ · e^(−λ·age) + β·hits"

claims.text: Each MemoryItem carries a tier T1, T2 or T3, the phase it was seen in, a snippet and a salience score
claims.quote:
Each `MemoryItem` carries a tier
  (T1/T2/T3), the phase it was seen in, a snippet, and a salience score

claims.text: A recurring narration or tool failure collapses onto one row and increments hits
claims.quote:
so a recurring one collapses onto one row (`hits` increments)
    instead of spamming the memory view

claims.text: 786 automated tests cover the implementation
claims.quote: The implementation is covered by 786 automated tests.

claims.text: The suite contains 786 tests across 53 modules
claims.quote: The suite contains 786 tests across 53 modules, mirroring the source tree roughly one-to-one.

claims.text: 10 terminal snapshot tests pin the rendered appearance
claims.quote: Ten terminal snapshot tests pin the rendered appearance.

claims.text: Correcting three extractor defects took one engagement from 0 to 8 evidence backed findings
claims.quote: Correcting them took one engagement from zero to eight evidence-backed findings across the affected tools.

claims.text: gobuster went from 0 to 5 findings because progress indicator escape sequences defeated the pattern
claims.quote: Progress-indicator escape sequences defeated the pattern; five real hits including an exposed installation script were being discarded

claims.text: whatweb went from 0 to 2 findings because no extractor existed
claims.quote: No extractor existed; results degraded to an opaque hash signal

claims.text: wafw00f went from 0 to 1 finding because it defaulted to a secure scheme against a plaintext only target
claims.quote: Defaulted to a secure scheme and failed against a plaintext-only target

claims.text: All three defects were invisible to a test suite written against clean sample output and visible at once against real output
claims.quote: All three defects were invisible to a test suite written against clean sample output, and all three were visible at once against real output from a real target.

claims.text: Buffered static costs 8.9 ms to append, 1.1 microseconds per token and 0.8 ms to render
claims.quote:
Buffered static (shipped)
8.9 ms
1.1 µs
0.8 ms

claims.text: Log widget rewrite costs 364.2 ms to append and 45.5 microseconds per token
claims.quote:
Log-widget rewrite
364.2 ms
45.5 µs
0.4 ms

claims.text: Naive static costs 793.3 ms to append and 99.2 microseconds per token
claims.quote:
Naive static
793.3 ms
99.2 µs
0.4 ms

claims.text: The benchmark streams 8000 tokens into one wrapping paragraph in a terminal 100 columns by 30 rows
claims.quote: The benchmark streams eight thousand tokens into one wrapping paragraph in a terminal of one hundred columns by thirty rows, under three strategies.

claims.text: The shipped strategy measures 1.4 microseconds at 4000 tokens and 1.1 microseconds at 8000, while the naive strategy climbs from 58 to 99 microseconds
claims.quote: measuring 1.4 microseconds at four thousand tokens and 1.1 microseconds at eight thousand, while the naive strategy climbs from 58 to 99 microseconds over the same range, which is quadratic in entry length

claims.text: Two headless runs produced 1 finding each, with first finding times of 2.9 s and 3.0 s
claims.quote:
Run
Findings
Time to first finding

1

claims.text: Identical finding counts and first finding times within a tenth of a second put the measurement inside the range needed to detect a change of consequence
claims.quote: Two runs against an unchanged codebase produced identical finding counts and first-finding times within a tenth of a second of each other, which puts the measurement well inside the range needed to detect a change of consequence.

claims.text: The audit scope was the full cism package of about 6500 lines of code
claims.quote: full `cism/` package (~6,500 LOC)

claims.text: Only CISM runs without sending engagement data off the machine
claims.quote:
Runs without sending engagement data off the machine
No
No
Yes

claims.text: Only CISM carries the tool output that justifies each finding
claims.quote:
Findings carry the tool output that justifies them
No
No
Yes

claims.text: Only CISM invalidates dependents when a precondition is disproved
claims.quote:
A disproved precondition invalidates its dependents
No
No
Yes

claims.text: Only CISM enforces scope before the process is created
claims.quote:
Scope enforced before the process is created
Not applicable
No

claims.text: A system that cannot run without a hosted endpoint is unavailable for engagements whose contracts forbid data egress
claims.quote: A system that cannot run without a hosted endpoint is unavailable for engagements whose contracts forbid data egress, however well it performs elsewhere.

claims.text: The model intermittently answers a tool offering turn by asking for information it already has
claims.quote: The model intermittently answers a turn that offers tools by asking for information it already has, for example requesting the target address when that address sits in both the instruction and the system prompt.

claims.text: A bounded retry was implemented and then reverted because a discarded attempt's text leaked into narration; six tests caught it
claims.quote: Six tests that assert exactly one narration and token sequence per turn caught it.

claims.text: The model invoked the port scanner with the literal placeholder token as the target argument
claims.quote: The same model separately invoked the port scanner with the literal placeholder token as the target argument instead of the address, producing a real tool call that failed at name resolution.

claims.text: When an early tool call produces no finding the phase never advances past reconnaissance and the operator gets no signal
claims.quote: When an early turn's tool call produces no usable finding, through either of the failures above, the phase never advances past reconnaissance.

claims.text: Offline validation against clean sample output is insufficient for this class of system
claims.quote: The most practical conclusion is that offline validation against clean sample output is insufficient for this class of system.

claims.text: Evaluation used a single target application and a single model family
claims.quote: Evaluation used a single target application and a single model family, so the results should not be generalized to other targets or models without repetition.

claims.text: Checkpointed state does not survive a process restart
claims.quote: Checkpointed state does not survive a process restart.

claims.text: Future work: make a discarded model attempt invisible to the event stream
claims.quote: Make a discarded model attempt invisible to the event stream, so a bounded retry on a turn with no tool calls becomes safe to ship.

claims.text: Future work: add an argument validation guardrail stage that rejects placeholder shaped arguments
claims.quote: Add an argument-validation guardrail stage that rejects placeholder-shaped and templated arguments before execution

claims.text: Future work: implement network egress control for the sandbox
claims.quote: Implement network egress control for the sandbox, so a tool cannot reach anything beyond the declared scope

claims.text: Future work: replace the dangerous argument denylist with an allowlist grammar per tool
claims.quote: Replace the dangerous-argument denylist with an allowlist grammar per tool

claims.text: The target is a containerized Damn Vulnerable Web Application on an isolated bridge network with scope limited to the target address alone
claims.quote: The target is a containerized Damn Vulnerable Web Application instance on an isolated bridge network, with its database initialized and its security level left at the image default.

claims.text: Three scripted instructions drive each engagement and each configuration is run twice
claims.quote: Three scripted instructions drive each engagement, covering reconnaissance, enumeration and injection testing, and each configuration is run twice.

claims.text: Inference comes from a local llama.cpp server hosting a quantized small model over its OpenAI compatible endpoint
claims.quote: Inference comes from a local llama.cpp server hosting a quantized small model, reached over its OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

claims.text: Manikandan owns the TUI, tool integration, deterministic extractors, sandboxing, guardrails, deployment, tests and CI
claims.quote: Manikandan: TUI, tool integration (nmap, hydra, gobuster, whatweb and wafw00f plus the offline dummy tools), deterministic extractors, sandboxing (Bubblewrap), guardrails implementation,

claims.text: Madhan owns SLM inferencing, the think act loop, DEPG maths, phase locking, LLM extractor backends and inference benchmarking
claims.quote: Madhane: SLM inferencing (llama.cpp or an OpenAI-compatible server, quantisation, context window), think-act loop (LangGraph), DEPG maths and implementation (reducer, SupportPolicy, settle()/prune()),

claims.text: Sushindh owns model testing, accuracy benchmarking, the ablation study, prompt QC, guardrail red teaming and the literature survey
claims.quote: Sushindh: model testing (tool-call and text-fallback reliability across SLMs), accuracy benchmarking (recall and precision on Juice Shop),

claims.text: The TUI is a pure consumer: nothing under cism/tui calls into LangGraph, llama.cpp or the scorer
claims.quote:
Nothing under
`cism/tui/` calls into LangGraph, llama.cpp, or the cross-encoder scorer, and
no widget ever calls the agent.

claims.text: SessionState never carries a key; it carries the name of the environment variable and whether it is set
claims.quote:
It carries the *name* of the
environment variable and a boolean saying whether it is set.

claims.text: A false positive costs one retype, a false negative leaks a key into a deliverable
claims.quote:
a false positive costs one retype, a false
negative leaks a key into a deliverable.

claims.text: Phase progression advanced one phase per any successful tool call, reaching reporting in about 5 calls
claims.quote: advances one phase per *any* successful tool call, so the agent reaches REPORTING in ~5 calls

claims.text: Compaction engages proactively once usage passes 0.75 of the budget
claims.quote: _PROACTIVE_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD = 0.75

claims.text: build_toolkit assembles 10 real tools: the 8 declared in catalog.yaml plus hydra and netcat
claims.quote: build_toolkit(CATALOG, [hydra, nc], EXTRACTORS)
